title: Lumen Foundry raises $1.2 billion Series D to build photonic AI accelerators
text:
Lumen Foundry raises $1.2 billion Series D to build photonic AI accelerators

Lumen Foundry, a developer of photonic chips for AI inference, today announced a $1.2 billion Series D financing that values the company at $9.8 billion after the new money.

The round was led by two existing investors and joined by a sovereign fund. Lumen Foundry said it will use the proceeds to finish its second chip, which it calls L2, and to reserve packaging capacity for 2 years.

The company said its first chip is in pilot use at 3 data-centre operators and that L2 is scheduled to reach customers in sample quantities within 9 months. It claimed L2 will use 70% less power per query than the systems those operators run today, a figure that has not been independently verified.

Lumen Foundry did not disclose its revenue, its losses, or the terms attached to the sovereign fund's investment. It has raised $2.1 billion in total.

Lumen Foundry is a private company. Its shares are not listed on any exchange and it said it has no current plan for a public offering.

The company named two risks: its chips depend on a single packaging supplier, and its power claim rests on its own tests.
